_note: The audit's check catalogue. The SKILL owns this; the dashboard renders it and must not restate it. `status` is the honest coverage position, and it is the single home of the porting backlog.

_status.scanner: Implemented in scanner/audit.js. Runs identically from a session and from the dashboard.
_status.session: Agent-layer. Only a full session run originates it — the dashboard's judgement pass FILTERS scanner candidates and never raises its own, so these do not run from the page.
_status.backlog: Documented here, implemented nowhere. Does not run from a session or the dashboard unless written by hand.
_status.rule: Not a check — a rule about how findings are ordered or scored.

dimensions.why: A raw value is a decision that cannot be changed centrally. It survives every rebrand untouched, and nothing about it announces that it was meant to be a token.

checks.text: Every non-zero padding, gap and per-corner radius is bound to a variable
checks.note: audit.js notes each raw padding and gap as on or off the spacing scale, and each radius against radius, naming the nearest step when off. An off-scale padding of 80 or more is filed as review — usually a progress or slider fill, which is a question, not a defect.

checks.text: Every visible fill and stroke colour is bound

Stroke weight is bound — read on the four per-side properties where a node has them, since the shorthand carries no binding there and reading it flags correct strokes; on the shorthand only where a node has no per-side weights (vectors, lines, ellipses)
Every text layer carries a text style and bound font family, size and weight
Every bound fill resolves to the collection the settings name as semantic, matched by name
checks.note: audit.js matches this collection by NAME (`t.collection !== COLL`): it states which collection a project intends fills to come from. Which LIBRARY a binding came from is the key check below, since two libraries can publish the same collection name.

checks.text: Every binding comes from a collection whose key the settings allow as allowedKeys
checks.note: audit.js resolves every bound property's collection and compares its KEY. Skipped when the settings carry no allowedKeys. Not yet control-passed live: that a teamLibrary collection key equals the imported collection's key is assumed.

checks.text: A text layer's fill comes from the text role the settings name as textRole, and a non-text layer's does not
checks.note: audit.js: a TEXT node bound to a colour whose path has no <textRole>/ segment, and any other node bound to one that has. No other role is inferred from node type. Skipped when the settings carry no textRole.

checks.text: A raw value serving a mechanism — a negative overlap, a fill driven by padding — is a question, not a defect
An unbound gap on a single-child frame: inert today, a defect the moment a second child arrives

dimensions.why: The variant grid is the component's public surface. A defect here is copied into every instance and cannot be fixed without breaking them.

checks.text: No unused component property. Figma ignores the whole component at publication when one is declared but applied to no layer — consumers never receive it, and the publish reports success

A layer's twins agree. Within one set, a layer wired to a text, instance-swap or boolean property in some variants and to nothing in others — the other direction of the unused-property check, which passes the moment one layer uses a property. Keyed by path and by what the layer is — its type, an instance's contents, and for a boolean whether it stands alone — with an ordinal for same-named siblings, never by name.
Axis order follows the project's grammar, with state-like axes last
checks.note: audit.js schema|axis-order|: the state axis last, the disabled axis before it, a project's firstAxis first (figma-standard rule 1). The order of the other axes is read by the reader.

checks.text: Boolean axes carry exactly two options, ordered default-first
checks.note: audit.js schema|bool-default|: a True/False axis with no recorded order lists its default first (figma-standard rule 1). That a boolean carries exactly two options is not checked.

checks.text: No stray options left behind by a rename
checks.note: Deliberately not checked yet: membership is a coverage question, not an ordering one, and needs its own ruling.

checks.text: Property names follow the project's pattern — text props, swap props, casing
checks.note: audit.js, from the settings, each skipped when its key is absent: a boolean property starts with booleanPrefix, and where it is set no variant starts with Is and no style boolean with Is or Has; a text property does not end with textPropertyAvoid unless textPropertyExceptions names it; a swap property does not end with swapAvoid; every name is in propertyCase.

checks.text: A size property is named, valued and drawn the way the settings say
checks.note: audit.js, from the settings: a size-like property (sizeAxisMatch) is named sizeAxis; its options sit on the recorded Size scale in its order; the options a component uses are one unbroken run of the scale; where sizeShared, one size name draws one height across components (a question, not a defect); a size value that draws nothing distinct is filed. Absent keys skip their part.

checks.text: No Figma default names anywhere: Frame 12, Rectangle 4, Component 1
An axis with a single option — no choice offered, usually a remnant, but removing one is breaking
An axis whose only effect is toggling one subtree's visibility should be a boolean
A sparse variant grid — only a finding when it breaks the file's own pattern
A layer name that is legal but misleading; only a reader can catch that

dimensions.why: The part users experience and the part least visible while designing, because the canvas shows every state at once and the product shows one at a time.

checks.text: Every non-rest state renders. A Press or Disabled variant identical to Rest is a product bug and leads the queue ahead of anything cosmetic
checks.note: Implemented in the scanner, though catalogued as agent-layer — the resting-state comparison is fully deterministic once the rulebook names the axis.

checks.text: Each state variant binds its own state's tokens
checks.note: audit.js states|token|: a Hover token in Press, or a resting token the Rest sibling does not carry on the same layer (figma-standard rule 48). Layers pair by name path; a state no token in the set names is skipped.

checks.text: Focus is indicated, and visibly differs from rest
The state axis uses the project's vocabulary, in the project's order
Coverage against the archetype — a state missing library-wide is conformance, missing on one component is a question

dimensions.why: What decides whether a component survives contact with real content. Invisible while it holds the placeholder text it was drawn with.

checks.text: Text hugs vertically. A fixed-height text node clips instead of reflowing — invisible at rest, and it fails in the locale nobody tested
No GROUP nodes inside a component: a group ignores the auto-layout everything around it obeys
A frame holding layers uses auto layout: without it an agent gets absolute positions it can only copy
checks.note: audit.js structure|no-autolayout (figma-standard rule 33); an overlay or illustration may be absolute by design, so it is a question.

checks.text: An overlay part such as a state layer is locked, stretched both ways, at 0,0 and its parent's size
checks.note: audit.js structure|overlay, from overlayComponents, a project's own rule; absent, not checked.

checks.text: An instance whose main component no longer exists — it keeps looking correct while it stops receiving updates

No name carries leading or trailing whitespace — a page, a component or a layer. It is invisible in the layers panel, so it survives indefinitely, and an exporter comparing names untrimmed turns one into a component the consuming repo cannot account for
No name carries a double space between words
Text a consumer would legitimately set is exposed as a text property
Detached frames on documentation pages that duplicate a real component
checks.note: probes.js FCA.detachedScan lists candidates by name; the reader confirms each by ancestry (figma-standard rule 27).

checks.text: Names follow the project's case convention — which case is the project's to state, never this skill's
checks.note: audit.js naming|layer-case|, naming|component-case and naming|value-case|, where propertyCase is sentence (figma-standard rule 18); a part's layer still carrying its whole name is naming|part-layer| (figma-standard rule 9).

checks.text: Open content uses the slot mechanism consistently; one responsibility per component set
Layers hidden without a property controlling them — dead weight, or a conditional the property model never captured
Disabled paints, strokes and effects: switched off in the panel, still in the array carrying a colour and a binding

dimensions.why: Raised from FigmaLint's 3 deliberately. The description is the only channel reaching someone who never opens the file, and the line naming what a component is built from is what stops it being reimplemented.

checks.text: Public components carry a non-empty, non-placeholder description
A public component's description carries Usage and Don't sections, and Code gen notes (a review); a slot part owes none
checks.note: audit.js metadata|guidance and metadata|guidance-code (figma-standard rule 25); runs only where the project names its internalPrefix. A variant whose description differs from its set's is metadata|variant-description.

checks.text: Private components carry one too — a compact sentence or two, not the full structure
checks.note: audit.js metadata|description raises a missing one as hygiene on a private part (figma-standard rule 25); whether it is compact rather than the full structure is the reader's.

checks.text: Composition is named. A composite component whose description omits what it contains is incomplete, whatever the project calls its headings
A description is not stale — checked against the current axes and properties, not just against emptiness
Property descriptions where the name alone does not carry the meaning
Dev Mode annotations on variants carrying spec detail prose cannot hold — a cursor rule, a timing, an ARIA role

dimensions.why: Structural checks only — the defects present or absent in the file itself. Never a substitute for a specialist audit, and the page says so rather than implying coverage it does not have.

checks.text: Focus indication exists on focusable components and differs visibly from rest
checks.note: audit.js accessibility|focus raises a state axis with no focusState option (figma-standard rule 39); states|… raises one that renders like Rest.

checks.text: Text-on-surface contrast against the project's floor, resolved in every mode — a pairing that passes in light and fails in dark is the finding
checks.note: audit.js accessibility|contrast: opaque surfaces in the mode each variant resolves to; other modes and translucent surfaces stay reviewed (figma-standard rule 32).

checks.text: Interactive target size against the project's minimum, or WCAG 2.2 AA's 24×24 where none is stated
checks.note: audit.js accessibility|target raises variants under minTarget as a review (figma-standard rule 26); probes.js FCA.sizes still lists them for the reader.

checks.text: Text size against the smallest step of the type scale
checks.note: probes.js FCA.sizes lists them; the reader drops disabled text (figma-standard rule 26).

checks.text: An interactive component with no text of its own carries its accessible name, as a text property or a Dev Mode annotation
checks.note: audit.js accessibility|name (figma-standard rule 40, WCAG 4.1.2).

dimensions.dimension: Three rules that outrank the tiers

checks.text: A defect a user can see — a state that does not render, a missing focus ring, text that will clip — leads the queue whatever its dimension
An unused property caps its component at 25 out of 100. Averaging it against good token coverage would report a healthy number for a component consumers never receive
A finding on every instance of something is evidence the check is wrong or the pattern is a house rule. It is investigated, not reported
